title: Mew went in right at the very end.
description:
All the free space left on the Pokémon Red and Green cartridge once the debug features were removed.

Mew went in right at the very end. Programmer Shigeki Morimoto said the cartridge was really full and there wasn't room for much more on there.

It was left in for possible use after launch. Morimoto said it was kept in case it suited some post-launch activity.

Mew turned up in some players' games. Morimoto: 'It looked like we planned all of this, but that wasn't the case.' Staff had been told not to tamper with a single bit after debugging ended.

Over 78,000 people entered to win Mew. CoroCoro Comic's April 1996 Legendary Pokémon Offer had just 20 winners.

Game Freak programmer who added Mew after the debug features were removed.

Sources:
- https://iwataasks.nintendo.com/interviews/ds/pokemon/0/0/ - Nintendo's own interview; Morimoto says Mew went in 'right at the very end' because the cartridge was really full, that removing debug features left 'a miniscule 300 bytes', that it was left in for possible post-launch use, and that a bug leaked it into some players' games.
- https://www.gamespot.com/articles/how-mew-saved-pokemon/1100-6490812/ - corroborated the 300 bytes and the programmer Shigeki Morimoto, and gave the April 1996 CoroCoro Legendary Pokemon Offer with 20 winners and over 78,000 entries.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mew_(Pok%C3%A9mon) - corroborated that Mew was added after debug features were removed, that the sprite was small and uncoloured for lack of space, and the CoroCoro offer figures.
